narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Patch Bay"**

Behind its front panel, the window is a rack-mounted patch bay. Day to day, a teammate sees only the front: a calm list of what the team library offers, what is new, and what they already have, with one action on each row. The bay itself sits under "Where installed": library assets are rows, places (this project, the folders above it, your user) are columns, and a round jack at each crossing shows where an asset is live. The panel is anodized near-black in three stepped tones, labels are engraved in small tracked caps, and the only light in the room comes from lamps: mint for what is installed, amber for what you are about to change, red for what is blocked. A thin amber cable runs from a folder's jack to the project jack it feeds, so inheritance is drawn rather than explained.

The metaphor lives in the visuals and in the code, not in the words. The interface says "Assets", "click a circle", "Add a library" and "Review and apply"; it never asks a teammate to know what a jack, patch or bay is. Density is that of a working tool: 14px body, hairline-ruled rows, a centered 52rem library column, and on the grid a matrix sized to its columns with one quiet legend line under it. Places, agents and layers never reach the everyday screens, and anything that is a setting rather than a state stays folded until asked for.

The dark panel is the default world. A daylight world (warm off-white panels, the same lamps deepened for paper) follows the system's light preference unless the person picks a theme; a small pill in the faceplate cycles Auto, Light and Dark and is remembered in the browser. Every token is redefined for daylight, so components never branch on theme. The system uses one sans for everything a person reads and monospace only for paths and commands, ships no icon fonts and no images except the tour's screenshots, and runs under a self-only content policy with no external fonts or scripts.
keyCharacteristics: Stepped panel tones and 1px hairlines carry all structure; one modal casts the only shadow.
Color is state: mint is installed or up to date, amber is new, pending or your next step, red is blocked.
Everyday screens (Library, Share, first setup) are one column of rows with one action each; the grid is a maintenance view.
The jack (22px circle) is the signature control, with seven legible states and a one-line legend under the grid.
Engraved small caps label the panel; they never act as headings or kickers.
Two authored motions: a new cable draws out of the folder jack in 200ms, and the tour's cursor glides to each click and rings it in amber.

rules.name: The Two Lamps Rule
rules.body: Mint says "this is installed" or "up to date"; amber says "this waits for you": something new, a pending change, the next step, or what you are touching. Neither appears as decoration, and mint never fills a button.

rules.name: The Lamp Text Rule
rules.body: Lamp-colored words use `amber-text` or `mint-text`, never the lamp tokens themselves, so they stay readable on paper as well as on the panel.

rules.name: The Token Rule
rules.body: Every color lives as a custom property on `:root`. A new surface extends that set; it does not introduce a raw hex.

rules.name: The Readable Ring Rule
rules.body: Every jack ring that identifies a state or a control holds at least 3:1 against the panel it sits on; fills may be dimmer, rings may not. Daylight does not meet it yet for amber: the pending-jack ring, focus outline, routing-bar border, active underlines and the strip lamp in `amber-light` measure 2.1 to 2.5:1 on the light panels.

rules.name: The Engraving Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked caps label a part of the panel: a control, the matrix corner, a library group, a list on the library home, an asset's kind or a row badge. They are never placed above a heading to introduce it.

rules.name: The Machine Text Rule
rules.body: Monospace means a machine path or command. Prose, names and buttons stay in the sans.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Every live count (asset totals, the routing summary, count chips) uses tabular numerals so it does not jitter as it changes.

rules.name: The Sized-to-Fit Rule
rules.body: The matrix is as wide as its columns and no wider. It is never stretched to fill the viewport.

rules.name: The Front Panel Rule
rules.body: Everyday screens (Library, Share, first setup) show no places, agents or layers. Each row carries one action: a Get button, or a "have" pill with a quiet Remove link. Places, agents and layers live under Where installed and Settings.

rules.name: The Folded Settings Rule
rules.body: The grid shows state; settings wait to be asked for. A place's agents read as one quiet line in its column head and open into toggles only for the column clicked; a filter that cannot narrow anything is not shown; extra folders, long descriptions and full paths stay folded behind a button, a click on the row, or a tooltip.

rules.name: The Flat Panel Rule
rules.body: Panels, bars and sheets are separated by tone and hairline, never by a drop shadow. Only a modal dialog casts one.

dos: **Do** show install state with the jack and its seven states, and keep the one-line legend directly under the matrix.
**Do** use the three panel tones and 1px hairlines for every separation; keep the matrix sized to its columns.
**Do** reserve Patch Amber for what waits for the person: new items, pending changes, the forward action, focus, the active tab and selection.
**Do** keep monospace for paths, commands and change lines only.
**Do** use tabular numerals for every count that updates live.
**Do** give each library row exactly one action: Get (primary amber only for new or updated items, quiet otherwise) or a mint "have" pill with a Remove link.
**Do** keep occasional row actions as links that appear on hover or focus where the device can hover.
**Do** summarize per-place settings in one quiet line and open their controls only on request, for one place at a time.
**Do** put status messages and pending changes in the bottom dock, stacked, so neither covers the other or the grid.
**Do** draw jack rings in Jack Ring, Mint Ring or a lamp color, never in a hairline tone.
**Do** use plain words in the interface ("circle", "install", "Review and apply"); keep the patch-bay vocabulary in visuals and class names.
**Do** use `amber-text` and `mint-text` for lamp-colored words, and define every new token in both worlds.
**Do** turn the cable, sheet and tour animations off under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, and keep state transitions at 160 to 220ms on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`.
donts: **Don't** fill a button, banner or decoration with mint; mint means installed.
**Don't** put a drop shadow on panels, bars or sheets; only a modal dialog casts one.
**Don't** place engraved small caps above a heading as a kicker or eyebrow.
**Don't** show places, agents or layers on Library, Share or first setup.
**Don't** use a circle for anything that is not a state lamp, a toggleable jack or a setup step number.
**Don't** float toasts over the grid or show a control that has nothing to choose between.
**Don't** add raw hex values in component rules; extend the `:root` custom properties.
**Don't** lay out card grids or stack lifted boxes inside panels; rows inside a panel are divided by hairlines, and a form opened from a row sits in a recessed page-tone well with 8px corners.
